focus: Overengineering: CI versus git hooks and workflows versus each other, including advisory jobs that never gate
answeredQuestions: Which workflows or jobs are overengineered, such as duplicates of pre-commit hooks or advisory jobs that never gate?

label: advisory-checks.yml runs three whole-repo checks on every PR and every push to main/skilled/**, with no path filter, and each step is silenced twice: continue-on-error plus an inner '|| true'/'|| echo' that already forces exit 0, so neither the run nor the step can ever be red; its trigger-index freshness check also shares the push trigger with trigger-index-rebuild.yml, which repairs the same index on the same push.

comment-hygiene.yml and agent-mirror-sync.yml re-run checkers the commit gate already runs (comment hygiene and check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs both run from the git pre-commit), and the workflows README states the duplication outright; the backstop is justified for forks and --no-verify commits, but neither workflow is path-filtered, so each pays a checkout and Node setup on every PR.

dispatch-enforcement-guard.yml provisions the hooks workspace and runs vitest with only a config path and no project, path or test-name filter, so a dispatch-specific guard pays for the whole hooks vitest tree on top of its two narrow node --test dispatch suites, while gate-inputs.yml and hooks-node-tests.yml already run the sibling hook test trees.

The same spec-kit install-and-build (npm ci plus tsc build plus runtime build) is repeated in seven workflows (changed-packet-validation, command-tree-parity twice, playbook-operator-contract, routing-registry-drift, spec-kit-check, strict-pass-freshness-report, trigger-index-rebuild), and several of them fire together on one change because gate-inputs is deliberately unfiltered and the rest carry overlapping path filters.

Exactly two workflows never gate: advisory-checks (three continue-on-error steps) and strict-pass-freshness-report (a continue-on-error derived-repair step inside a report that already cannot fail); inside the weekly report a fifty-line baseline round trip through gh run list, gh run download and a parse exists only to reclassify rows as regressions and print one warning.

naming-standard-guard.yml, sk-doc-rename-harness.yml and sk-doc-script-tests.yml each pip-install pytest==8.4.2 with no cache (two also pin pyyaml==6.0.3), on path-filtered PR and push events, so one cache key or one shared composite action replaces three repeated installs.

There is no pre-push hook: pre-push appears nowhere in the hooks README and the commit-hook folder carries a single pre-commit, so every push-range and whole-history check is structurally CI-only, which is the documented reason message-contract.yml exists; the repo-wide absence claim is inferred because .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/ was not enumerated this iteration.

direction: Treat trigger-index-rebuild.yml's two-job bundle handoff (upload a one-commit bundle, push from a fresh runner) as overengineering to simplify away
reason: The split exists for token isolation: the rebuild job holds no secret and no write scope and the push job runs no repository code, documented in the workflows README. Simplifying it would put the write token beside code that just generated content.

direction: Delete comment-hygiene.yml and agent-mirror-sync.yml because the pre-commit hook already runs the same checkers
reason: A fork pull request never runs the fork's hooks and --no-verify bypasses them, so the CI copies are the only coverage on those paths; the actionable defect is the missing path filter, not the workflow's existence.

Two of its three checks (doc-model reference drift and trigger-index freshness) have no local equivalent and no other whole-repo home; the cost problem is the unfiltered trigger plus the redundant double suppression, both fixable without removing the checks.
